entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus directing the authorities to award compensation to the petitioners as per the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act').
2.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Section 24(1)(a) of the Act reads as follows:

1 "24.

entities.text: Ram Dhani Patel And 4 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Land acquisition process under Act No.1 of 1894 shall be deemed to have lapsed in certain cases.- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act

, in any case of land acquisition proceedings initiated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (1 of 1894),-
(a) where no award under Section 11 of the said Land Acquisition Act has been made,
then, all provisions of this Act relating to the determination of compensation shall apply."

3. A perusal of the averments made in the writ petition and the documents annexed therewith reveals that the land of the petitioners was acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Notification under Section 4 was published on 22.07.2002 followed by declaration under Section 6 dated 12.05.2003.

The respondents invoked the provisions of Section 17(1) of the Act,
while issuing declaration under Section 6 and, therefore, possession was taken even before the award was made.
4. According to respondent no.5, the state after taking possession delivered the same to it on 10.05.2005 and the name of respondent no.5 was recorded in the revenue records on 11.02.2011.
Respondent no.5 had deposited Rs.16,48,59,368/-, as compensation amount before the Special Land Acquisition Officer on 04.06.2005.
The compensation has been received by 1036 tenure holders out of 1774 tenure holders.
Most of the tenure holders were paid compensation under the provisions of Karar Niyamawali, 1997.

5. According to respondent no.5, compensation of 115.534 hectare has already been received by the tenure holders and the rest is lying with the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
6. Annexure-3 to the writ petition reveals that the father of the petitioners, to whom the land originally belonged, was paid Rs.1,67,476/-, as compensation in the year 2004.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner does not dispute that the said amount was paid to him under the Karar Niyamawali, 1997.

He submits that the aforesaid amount is only half amount of the compensation actually payable to him, however, he has not brought on record any evidence to prove the amount at which the agreement took place between the parties.
8. Having regard to the aforesaid admitted fact, we are of the opinion that the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of the new Act would not be attracted.

It is left open to the petitioners to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer about the alleged remaining claim and in which event, respondent no.3 will examine the claim and will take appropriate decision in accordance with law within eight weeks from the date, a copy of the instant order alongwith claim is made before him.
9. The petition stands disposed of accordingly.
(Kshitij Shailendra, J) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, A.C.J.) Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Ankit.
